classification.difficultyReason: Use the specified launch-point origin, substitute y=-h and apply the quadratic formula, retaining the positive root.

content.prompt:
A projectile is launched from a point at height $h$ above the ground (origin at the launch point) with speed $V$ at angle $\theta$. Show it lands after
$$t=\frac{V\sin\theta+\sqrt{V^2\sin^2\theta+2gh}}{g}.$$

answer.worked:
With the origin at the launch point,
$$y=-\frac12gt^2+V\sin\theta\,t.$$
At landing, $y=-h$, so
$$\begin{aligned}-h&=-\frac12gt^2+V\sin\theta\,t,\\\frac12gt^2-V\sin\theta\,t-h&=0,\\gt^2-2V\sin\theta\,t-2gh&=0.\end{aligned}$$
Taking the positive root, since $h>0$ and the landing time is positive,
$$\begin{aligned}t&=\frac{2V\sin\theta+\sqrt{4V^2\sin^2\theta+8gh}}{2g},\\t&=\frac{V\sin\theta+\sqrt{V^2\sin^2\theta+2gh}}{g}.\end{aligned}$$
